//: DO NOT EDIT THIS FILE before reading the comments below:
This is the default configuration for Tiny Tapeout projects. It should fit most designs.
If you change it, please make sure you understand what you are doing. We are not responsible
if your project fails because of a bad configuration.
!!! DO NOT EDIT THIS FILE unless you know what you are doing !!!
If you get stuck with this config, please open an issue or get in touch via the discord.
Here are some of the variables you may want to change:
PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT - You can increase this if Global Placement fails with error GPL-0302.
Users have reported that values up to 80 worked well for them.
Routability-driven placement off: the GitHub build diverged (GPL-0307) in its inflation phase; routing has plenty of room (32 % usage, 0 overflow)
Keep the hierarchical instance names (u_eng0.alu._1234_) after synthesis: needed to tell which module a cell came from

The IHP CMOS5L LibreLane default is SYNTH_STRATEGY DELAY 4, which makes the netlist about 35 % larger (21.5k instead of 15.7k cells with the ALU/CRC units) and unroutable on four metal layers; the 20 ns clock has several ns of slack, so optimise for area

Floorplan (compact symmetric, run tt10c; docs/TEST_RESULTS.md 8.4): both SRAM macros on the bottom edge, mirrored (FS) so their signal pins face up into the core, at x = 149.92 and 689.44 (whole stripe pitches of 44.96 um from the proven x = 60: a shift by 2 x 11.24 put a stripe into the macro's middle section, Metal4 spacing error M4.b in tt8b). The SRAM blocks Metal1-3 and we block Metal4 over it, so with only Metal2-Metal4 for signals a macro is a wall: it must not sit under the chip pins (top edge, x 30-191) or leave pockets of cells. y = 13.78 leaves no cell rows below the macro (vertical halo 10 um); the horizontal halo of 17 um leaves no sliver rows (tt8b: 42 rows 1.9 um wide broke the precheck pin check)

Engine fences (step Project.ModuleRegions, package librelane_plugin_project): each engine in a column the width of its SRAM plus halo, management / SPI / pin manager in the 89 um gap between them; removed after global placement. Timing-driven placement with fence regions needs PL_KEEP_RESIZE_BELOW_OVERFLOW 0 (else GPL-0316 crash: buffers the resizer adds during the timing-driven iterations have no place in the regions' bin grids)
Magic DRC reports about 116k errors that come from the SRAM macros' own layout (docs/TT_FLOW_RESULTS.md); the foundry KLayout DRC of the TT precheck is the real check

Hold: repair once after CTS. A repair after global routing (RUN_POST_GRT_*) inserted buffers into routed areas and every run that used it ended with routing violations (tt6b, tt6g); the hold uncertainty is split in pnr.sdc instead

Own SDC: same as LibreLane's base.sdc but with 0.1 ns clock uncertainty for hold instead of 0.25 ns (0.25 + margin made 1,906 flop-to-flop paths fail hold in the fast corner: 4,260 hold buffers, +20 % cell area)
Timing-driven placement (off by default): the critical path had a 213 fF net driven by a nand4_1 (1.7 ns)
CLOCK_PERIOD - Increase this in case you are getting setup time violations.

The value is in nanoseconds, so 20ns == 50MHz. Signoff at 50 MHz in all corners (tt10c: slow corner 1.08 V / 125 C +0.18 ns, typical +7.6 ns), after the pipelined CRC unit and the two register read ports (docs/TEST_RESULTS.md 8.4)
Hold slack margin - Increase them in case you are getting hold violations.
RUN_LINTER, LINTER_INCLUDE_PDK_MODELS - Disabling the linter is not recommended!
If you need a custom clock configuration, read the following documentation first:
https://tinytapeout.com/faq/#how-can-i-map-an-additional-external-clock-to-one-of-the-gpios
Configuration docs: https://librelane.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/configuration.html

Save some time
Don't put clock buffers on the outputs
Reduce wasted space
Absolute die size
Clock
Don't generate power rings
MAGIC_DEF_LABELS may cause issues with LVS
Only export pin area in LEF (without any connected nets)
stripes deliberately overlap the SRAM Metal4 power pins (same net); Magic flags that as an illegal overlap, LVS verifies it

SRAM timing: one model per corner (*_typ_*, *_fast_*, *_slow_*). LibreLane loads every key that matches the corner name, and all IHP corners start with nom_, so the old keys (nom_*, min_*, max_*) loaded the typical model everywhere: the slow corner saw a 3.05 ns SRAM clock-to-output instead of 5.13 ns
